slides.title: How can I make my writing less messy?
slides.body: Let's find out.
slides.notes: Ask: What makes writing look messy? Why do small mistakes matter?

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Most of your writing errors come from punctuation and capitalisation.
  • Fixing these will make your writing clearer and more professional.

slides.title: Instructions
slides.body: Each sentence has errors in punctuation or capitalisation. Circle each error. Write the correction above it.
slides.notes: Demo on the board: Show how to circle 'i' and write 'I' above it. Show worksheet task 1.

slides.title: Example
slides.body: i went to the beach yesterday.
slides.notes: CCQ: Why is 'i' wrong? What should it be? (Answer: 'I' is always capitalised.)

slides.title: Example
slides.body: I went to the beach yesterday. The pronoun I is always capitalised.

slides.title: Task 1
slides.body:
Now fix all the errors in questions 1-10.

Question 1 has 2 errors.
slides.notes: Give 5 min. Students work independently from the worksheet.

slides.title: Question 1 — Spot the error
slides.body: **i** think that learning **english** will help me get a better job.

slides.title: Question 1 — Corrected
slides.body: I think that learning English will help me get a better job.

slides.title: Question 2 — Spot the error
slides.body: The company hired a new **Manager** yesterday.

slides.title: Question 2 — Corrected
slides.body: The company hired a new manager yesterday.

slides.title: Question 3 — Spot the error
slides.body: She was born in Chiang Mai , Thailand.

slides.title: Question 3 — Corrected
slides.body: She was born in Chiang Mai, Thailand.

slides.title: Question 4 — Spot the error
slides.body: Even though the exam was difficult **M**ost students passed.

slides.title: Question 4 — Corrected
slides.body: Even though the exam was difficult, most students passed.

slides.title: Question 5 — Spot the error
slides.body: My grandfather who is 68 years old still works as a **Teacher**.

slides.title: Question 5 — Corrected
slides.body: My grandfather, who is 68 years old, still works as a teacher.

slides.title: Question 6 — Spot the error
slides.body: In my opinion **T**he city council should improve public transport.

slides.title: Question 6 — Corrected
slides.body: In my opinion, the city council should improve public transport.

slides.title: Question 7 — Spot the error
slides.body: The famous author Stephen King has written over 60 novels.

slides.title: Question 7 — Corrected
slides.body: The famous author, Stephen King, has written over 60 novels.

slides.title: Question 8 — Spot the error
slides.body: The students were tired but they continued working.

slides.title: Question 8 — Corrected
slides.body: The students were tired, but they continued working.

slides.title: Question 9 — Spot the error
slides.body: She wanted to attend the conference however she couldn't get time off.

slides.title: Question 9 — Corrected
slides.body: She wanted to attend the conference; however, she couldn't get time off.

slides.title: Question 10 — Spot the error
slides.body: Many **Students** find English grammar challenging at first.

slides.title: Question 10 — Corrected
slides.body: Many students find English grammar challenging at first.

slides.title: Task 2 — Recall
slides.body: Each box shows an error from Task 1. Explain the rule that was broken. Write **one complete sentence**.
slides.notes: Demo: 'i' → 'The pronoun I must always be capitalised.' Give 5 min for all four rules.

slides.title: Rule — The pronoun **I**
slides.body: The pronoun I must always be capitalised. Never write **i**.
slides.notes: CCQ: What about 'my', 'me', 'mine'? (Those are not capitalised. Only 'I'.)

slides.title: Rule 1 — Common nouns
slides.body: Don't capitalise common nouns. Only proper nouns (names, places) need capitals. teacher, manager, students → lowercase.
slides.notes: CCQ: Is 'English' a common or proper noun? (Proper - nationality/language.) CCQ: Is 'manager' proper? (No - it's a job title.)

slides.title: Rule 2 — Comma spacing
slides.body: Never put a space **before** a comma. Always put a space **after** a comma. Chiang Mai, Thailand ✓
slides.notes: CCQ: Which is correct: 'word , word' or 'word, word'? (Second one.)

slides.title: Rule 3 — After an introduction
slides.body: After an introductory phrase, use a **comma**. Then use a **lowercase** letter. In my opinion, the city council ✓
slides.notes: CCQ: What comes after the comma? (A lowercase letter, not uppercase.)

slides.title: Rule 4 — Connecting with **However**
slides.body: Use a **semicolon** before **however**. Use a **comma** after it. ...the conference ; however, she couldn't...
slides.notes: CCQ: What punctuation goes BEFORE 'however'? (Semicolon.) What goes AFTER? (Comma.)

slides.title: Task 3 — Use
slides.body:
Write a paragraph about **a difficult decision** you had to make.

Focus on correct punctuation and capitalisation.

~70 words.
slides.notes: Give 8 min. Circulate and help. Remind students to check their work before handing in.

slides.title: Checklist
slides.body:
• A sentence starting with although, because, or while
  • A sentence with extra information in commas
  • Correct comma before and or but
  • The word however used correctly
slides.notes: Before they start, review each item. Ask for an example sentence for each.
